title: Latency, Bandwidth & Throughput: Know the Difference

scenes.say: Is a bigger network pipe always faster? Or does latency slow you down?

scenes.label: Bandwidth
scenes.sub: The size of the pipe—how much data can flow at once.
scenes.say: Bandwidth is the size of your network pipe. It’s the max capacity, not what you actually get.
Latency is the round-trip time. Throughput is what you really get. Loss means missing packets. Jitter is when latency keeps changing.
A huge pipe doesn’t help if round trips are slow or packets vanish. High latency or loss can kill your throughput, no matter the bandwidth.

scenes.question: What fixes slow file copies?
scenes.right: Check latency, loss, and TCP window size. Bandwidth alone may not help.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: If a file copy is slow, do you just upgrade bandwidth? Not always. Latency, loss, and TCP window size can be the real blockers.
